note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Give a customer the promised delivery date. A shipment booked before 14:00 on a business day ships that day; otherwise it ships the next business day. Delivery is the given number of business days after the ship day. Business days are Monday to Friday, except the listed public holidays.
facts: Made-up examples, with 2026-07-06 as a public holiday: booked Friday 2026-07-03 at 15:00 with 2 days in transit ships Tuesday 2026-07-07 and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-09. Booked Wednesday 2026-07-01 at 09:00 with 1 day in transit ships that day and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-02.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Given a booking date and time, a number of transit days and a list of public holidays, the system returns a promised ship date and delivery date.
REQ-2: A business day is Monday to Friday, excluding listed public holidays. Saturdays, Sundays and listed holidays are never ship or delivery days.
REQ-3: A booking made before 14:00 on a business day ships that same day. A booking at or after 14:00, or on any non-business day, ships on the next business day. Treating exactly 14:00 as late is an assumption, since the brief says only 'before 14:00'.
REQ-4: The delivery date is the ship date plus the given number of business days, counting only business days.
REQ-5: Open questions to confirm: which time zone the 14:00 cutoff uses, whether 0 transit days is allowed, and who maintains the holiday list.
AC-1: With 2026-07-06 as a holiday, a booking on Friday 2026-07-03 at 15:00 with 2 transit days ships Tuesday 2026-07-07 and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-09. This is after the cutoff; Saturday, Sunday and the Monday holiday are skipped, and delivery falls on Wednesday 08 then Thursday 09.
AC-2: A booking on Wednesday 2026-07-01 at 09:00 with 1 transit day ships Wednesday 2026-07-01 and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-02.
AC-3: Under the REQ-3 assumption, a booking on Wednesday 2026-07-01 at exactly 14:00 with 1 transit day ships Thursday 2026-07-02 and is delivered Friday 2026-07-03.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: A shipment booked before 14:00 on a business day ships that day; otherwise it ships the next business day.
REQ-2: The promised delivery date is the given number of business days after the ship day.
REQ-3: Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding listed public holidays.
AC-1: Booked Friday 2026-07-03 at 15:00 with 2 days in transit ships Tuesday 2026-07-07 and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-09; 2026-07-06 is a public holiday.
AC-2: Booked Wednesday 2026-07-01 at 09:00 with 1 day in transit ships that day and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-02.

findings.title: Exact cutoff is not assumed
findings.detail: The brief ships that day only when booked before 14:00 on a business day, and otherwise ships the next business day. Exactly 14:00 fails the before test, so the otherwise clause already makes it late. Calling that an assumption is incorrect.
findings.quote: Treating exactly 14:00 as late is an assumption, since the brief says only 'before 14:00'.

reviewOfA.strengths: AC-1 and AC-2 correctly restate both given examples, including ship date 2026-07-07 and delivery date 2026-07-09.

reviewOfB.strengths: The requirements restate the brief faithfully, and both acceptance criteria check out: Friday 2026-07-03 is a Friday, and a 15:00 booking skips the weekend and the 2026-07-06 holiday to ship Tuesday 2026-07-07 and arrive Thursday 2026-07-09; Wednesday 2026-07-01 at 09:00 ships that day and arrives Thursday 2026-07-02.

build.contract: promiseDelivery(input) where input = { bookedAt: string (local wall-clock booking date and time, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", such as "2026-07-03T15:00", with no time zone), transitDays: number (a whole number of business days, 0 or more), holidays: string[] (public holiday dates as "YYYY-MM-DD"; may be empty) }. Returns { shipDate: string ("YYYY-MM-DD"), deliveryDate: string ("YYYY-MM-DD") }. The 14:00 cutoff is compared against the wall-clock time in bookedAt exactly as given; the function does no time zone conversion, and the caller must supply bookedAt in the cutoff's time zone. A bookedAt time of 13:59 or earlier on a business day ships that day; 14:00 or later, or any time on a non-business day, ships the next business day. deliveryDate is transitDays business days after shipDate; when transitDays is 0, deliveryDate equals shipDate. promiseDelivery throws an Error whose message is "invalid transitDays" if transitDays is negative or not a whole number. promiseDelivery throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field. isBusinessDay(date, holidays) where date is a string ("YYYY-MM-DD") and holidays is a string[] ("YYYY-MM-DD"). Returns boolean: true only if date is Monday to Friday and not in holidays.

architecture.draft:
Components: one pure module exporting promiseDelivery(input) and isBusinessDay(date, holidays), with no I/O, clock or time zone use, plus one unit test file.
isBusinessDay: parse YYYY-MM-DD with Date.UTC and read getUTCDay so the host time zone cannot shift the day. Return true only for Mon-Fri dates not in holidays (exact string match, using a Set).
nextBusinessDay(date, holidays): a private helper that adds one UTC day until isBusinessDay is true, then formats the result as YYYY-MM-DD.
promiseDelivery steps: (1) reject any key other than bookedAt, transitDays or holidays with "unknown field: <name>"; (2) throw "invalid transitDays" unless Number.isInteger(transitDays) and transitDays >= 0; (3) split bookedAt at T into date and HH:MM; (4) shipDate is the booking date if it is a business day and HH:MM < "14:00", otherwise nextBusinessDay(date); (5) deliveryDate starts at shipDate and advances with nextBusinessDay transitDays times, so 0 returns shipDate.
Data: inputs and outputs are plain strings and numbers as in the contract. There is no stored state. The holiday list is supplied by the caller (who maintains it is still open, REQ-5).
Time zone: the cutoff is compared against the wall clock in bookedAt as given. The caller converts to the cutoff zone; that zone is still open in REQ-5.
Tests: AC-1 Fri 2026-07-03 15:00, 2 days, holiday 2026-07-06 gives ship 2026-07-07, delivery 2026-07-09. AC-2 Wed 2026-07-01 09:00, 1 day gives 2026-07-01 and 2026-07-02. AC-3 Wed 2026-07-01 14:00, 1 day gives 2026-07-02 and 2026-07-03. Also cover: 13:59, a weekend booking, transitDays 0, the two error messages, and an empty holidays list. Weekdays checked: 2026-07-01 is a Wednesday.
File fence (assumed paths, confirm against the repo): src/promiseDelivery.js (new) and test/promiseDelivery.test.js (new). No other files may change.
Out of scope: holiday list maintenance, time zone conversion, and validating the bookedAt format (the contract does not define it).

Strengths: UTC weekday checks, the 14:00 cutoff, holiday skips, and transit-day counting match the acceptance criteria, including the exact 14:00 boundary.

code.summary:
This is one pure expression that returns exactly { promiseDelivery, isBusinessDay }. It does no I/O and does not use the clock or the host time zone.

isBusinessDay reads the weekday with Date.UTC and getUTCDay. It returns true only for Monday to Friday dates that are not in the holidays list, using an exact string match through a Set.

promiseDelivery checks the input in this order:
- It throws "unknown field: <name>" for any key other than bookedAt, transitDays or holidays.
- It then throws "invalid transitDays" unless transitDays is a whole number and 0 or more.

It splits bookedAt at T and compares the HH:MM text with "14:00":
- A booking at 13:59 or earlier on a business day ships that day.
- Otherwise the ship date moves forward one day at a time to the next business day.

Delivery then advances transitDays business days from the ship date, so 0 transit days returns the ship date.

I hand-traced the three acceptance cases (I did not run the code):
- AC-1 ships 2026-07-07 and delivers 2026-07-09. It skips Saturday 07-04, Sunday 07-05 and the Monday 07-06 holiday.
- AC-2 gives 2026-07-01 and 2026-07-02.
- AC-3 at exactly 14:00 gives 2026-07-02 and 2026-07-03.

I also confirmed that 2026-07-01 is a Wednesday: it is day 182 of a year that starts on a Thursday.

Three points remain open from REQ-5: which time zone the cutoff uses (the caller supplies local wall-clock time), whether 0 transit days is allowed, and who maintains the holiday list. Checking the bookedAt format is out of scope.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: UTC date math and a strict before-14:00 check match every acceptance case, including the Monday holiday skip, same-day ship before cutoff, and zero transit days.
code.resolutions: No defects found; UTC date math and strict before-14:00 check match all acceptance cases. applied: Agreed after checking independently. 2026-07-03 is a Friday. At 15:00 it ships after skipping Sat 07-04, Sun 07-05 and the 07-06 holiday, so it ships Tue 07-07 and is delivered Thu 07-09 with 2 days. Wed 07-01 at 09:00 ships 07-01 and is delivered 07-02. At exactly 14:00 it ships Thu 07-02 and is delivered Fri 07-03. With 0 transit days, deliveryDate equals shipDate. The code also enforces the error messages for unknown fields and invalid transitDays. The code is unchanged.
